headline: Eureka Metals wants $499,134 from shareholders at a penny a share

sources.title: Eureka Metals Corp. Announces Rights Offering and Proposed Share Consolidation
Eureka Metals Corp. Initiates $0.01 Per Share Rights Offering and Plans Up-to-6-for-1 Share Consolidation

unverified_claims: Eureka's own account of its planned use of proceeds for exploration, property and administrative costs
brief: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA), a mineral explorer with titanium, vanadium and scandium projects in Quebec and British Columbia, has launched a rights offering to raise up to $499,134. Shareholders of record on November 6 get one transferable right per share, each exercisable for one pre-consolidation share at $0.01.

Rights expire December 1 at 4 p.m. Toronto time, with closing expected around December 2. Eureka separately plans to consolidate its shares on a ratio of up to six-for-one, which the board will finalize; at the maximum ratio the company would have about 16.6 million shares outstanding after both steps.

Odyssey Trust Company is acting as rights agent. Net proceeds, combined with existing working capital, are earmarked for exploration and property costs, general and administrative expenses and unallocated working capital, the company said.
body: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA) (OTCQB: UREKF) (FSE: S580), a Canadian mineral explorer holding titanium, vanadium, scandium and other polymetallic projects in Quebec and British Columbia, has launched a rights offering to raise up to $499,134. Holders of common shares as of November 6, 2026 will receive one transferable right for each share held.

Each right entitles its holder to subscribe for one pre-consolidation common share at $0.01. Rights expire December 1, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Toronto time, and the company expects the offering to close on or about December 2, 2026. Odyssey Trust Company is acting as rights agent.

Eureka separately proposes to consolidate its shares on a basis of up to six pre-consolidation shares for every one post-consolidation share, with the final ratio to be set by the board. The company had 49,913,367 shares outstanding before the offering; if every right is exercised, that would roughly double to about 99,826,734 shares before the consolidation is applied.

At the maximum six-for-one ratio and full exercise of the rights, Eureka would have approximately 16,637,789 shares outstanding following both the offering and the consolidation. The company says the consolidation remains subject to Canadian Securities Exchange approval, and shares are expected to continue trading under the ticker ERKA.

The company said net proceeds from the rights offering, combined with its existing working capital, are expected to fund exploration and property costs, general and administrative expenses, and unallocated working capital. The offering is open to shareholders in all Canadian provinces and territories and in select international jurisdictions, excluding the United States.

The release does not state whether the dollar figures in the offering are Canadian or U.S. currency. Eureka is a Canadian company listed primarily on the Canadian Securities Exchange, with secondary listings on the OTCQB in the United States and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.
